name: Japanese
modelReview: built 2026-11-12 by Claude Fable 5.2 from the questionnaire answers, lexicon and visible paradigms, after two schedule reads and three blind fluency reads of the rows; 153 of 153 held-out rows pass on the first judged run (tooling/experiments/renderer-process/ja-acceptance.md); audited 2026-11-13 by Claude Fable 5.2, which read some 3,500 rendered sentences against their fire times and the renderer against the answers, then repaired seven forms that could be taken to fire differently (rules and rows first); the new forms have had no blind fluency read; revised 2026-11-13 by Claude Fable 5.2 in a second round: the renderer now reads the core's calendar and set facts (months and years a day can fire in, sets with no end, runs and cadences together) and holds no month lengths or year bounds of its own; every trap found across the eight languages was run and read; the rule book was read section by section beside the usage notes (src/lang/ja/usage.md) and its departures recorded in its last section (平日 dropped, nearest-weekday forms said as a day and where it moves, 正午, weekday ranges across Sunday, schedules that never run); the forms changed in either round have had no blind fluency read; 2026-11-13: says when both day fields must match (a day field written from a star beside a restricted one, as in Vixie cron), in rows, rule and renderer written by Claude Sonnet 5.5 from this rule book's seed and reviewed by Claude Fable 5.2; a blind Sonnet reader told these sentences from the union's 16 times of 16, and none has had a blind fluency read; amended 2026-11-14 by Claude Opus 5.5 on the maintainer's rulings: an hour cadence that tiles the day is said by its interval (2時間ごと; 6時間ごと), from its first time where that is not 0:00 (1:00から2時間ごと; 0:30から2時間ごと), with no end and no 毎日, while one that does not tile keeps both ends; such hours as stretches are 偶数の時間帯 or 奇数の時間帯 for every second hour and N時間ごとに1時間ずつ、その間は… otherwise, with a cadence of minutes from the hour said by its interval after them; no bracket shows a series of numbers (the first hours after 偶数の時間帯, the first years after a cadence of years); a tiling cadence with hours left out is the same cadence, said bare with the exception after it (2時間ごと（8:00を除く）; 8時台を除く偶数の時間帯に1分ごと); beside a day, a month or a year a bare cadence (of hours that tile the day, or of minutes or seconds through every hour) takes a comma and neither 終日 nor 毎日 (毎月1日、2時間ごと; 毎月1日、15分ごと; 毎年6月、5分ごと), the reader evidence for 終日 being overruled as a preference for added words, while a first time keeps its join (毎月1日の1:00から2時間ごと); an exception never takes back the first or last value of a cadence, idiom or range (偶数月（2月を除く） is now 4月・6月・8月・10月・12月); the rule book was amended first and every affected row rewritten by hand before the renderer changed; nothing was blind-read; 2026-11-14, released stable on the full reading check: all 767 rows read by three Sonnet 5.5 readers briefed only in the language (5546 questions about moments, scored against an answer key that shares no code with the library), and each of the 10 questions most readers got wrong asked again alone of three Sonnet 5.5 and three Opus 5.5 readers: none was still misread by most readers of both (tooling/scripts/reading/recheck.mjs); 2026-11-19, every second day under named months is said by the days it reaches in the months it fires in, not by the range written, so that one schedule has one sentence (`0 9 1-29/2 6 *` and `0 9 */2 6 *` are both 毎年6月の奇数日の9:00; answers 5.1, rows first); later on 2026-11-19, every set of days is judged against the days the months it fires in have (core monthLengths and daysByMonths), so the same days are one sentence however spelled (`1-14,16-30` and `1-14,16-31` in June are both 15日を除く毎年6月の毎日; `L` and `30` in June both 毎年6月30日; `LW` and `30W` in June alike) and no sentence gives a month a day it lacks (`*/3` in April and July is …31日（31日は7月のみ）; `30,31` in April and May is 毎年4月30日・5月30日・5月31日); answers 3.4, 4.4, 5.1, 5.7 amended first and rows by hand
